prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S034: The Raw Water Screen Channel sends the Rake Torque Snapshot at the end of each cleaning cycle to preserve the recorded loading condition.
S035: If the Raw Water Screen Channel shows rapid level change, plant staff verify that the cleaning mechanism is running and that the River Intake Pump Station is not drawing the channel down too quickly.
S036: A high-high level condition at the Raw Water Screen Channel requires immediate field confirmation because it may indicate restricted passage, failed cleaning, or abnormal river backwater.
S037: Raw-water quality triggers include high turbidity, unusual color, odor complaints from field staff, visible sheen, algae accumulation, and rapid temperature change.
S038: When a raw-water quality trigger occurs, the Chief Operator determines whether to adjust pumping rate, request additional laboratory testing, or increase downstream process monitoring.
S039: The Laboratory Technician supports intake decisions by prioritizing raw-water checks when storm runoff or an abnormal visual condition is reported.
S040: The Coagulant Dosing Skid is placed under closer observation when intake turbidity changes faster than the normal control response can stabilize.
S041: The North Filter Gallery and South Filter Gallery are advised when incoming water quality is expected to shorten filter run time or increase solids loading.
S042: Pump permissives at the River Intake Pump Station include adequate suction level, available discharge path, healthy motor status, open isolation valves, and absence of active protective trips.
S043: A pump is not permitted to start when the Raw Water Screen Channel downstream level is below the established low-level limit.
S044: A pump start is also blocked when the associated drive reports a fault, when local control is selected, or when a safety interlock is not proven.
S045: If a permissive is lost during operation, the control system either alarms the condition or stops the affected pump according to the severity of the signal.
S046: The Chief Operator may authorize temporary manual operation only when the cause is understood, the equipment can be observed, and the risk to treatment continuity is acceptable.
S047: The SCADA Historian Server retains river level, screen differential, pump status, and raw-water quality trends for operating review and event reconstruction.
S048: The Duty Engineer reviews storm forecasts and river-stage information when a prolonged debris event or high-flow period is expected.
S049: The Distribution Dispatcher is notified when intake limitations could reduce the ability of the High Service Pump Header to meet planned system demand.
S050: The Clearwell Level Controller is watched during intake restrictions because storage level provides the main buffer between reduced raw-water supply and treated-water delivery.
S051: Return to normal service occurs after river level, screen differential, raw-water quality, and pump cycling have stabilized for a period accepted by the Chief Operator.
S052: After a storm event, the Maintenance Planner reviews intake equipment condition and schedules cleaning or inspection work needed to restore reliable operation.
S053: Following a storm-related recovery, control of coagulation and filtration returns to normal only after raw-water quality trends support stable chemical feed and predictable filter loading.
S054: The Chief Operator establishes the starting coagulant dose from recent turbidity, color, alkalinity, pH, temperature, and bench-scale treatment observations.
S055: The Coagulant Dosing Skid, known locally as Marigold, meters the primary coagulant under automatic control during routine operation.
S056: The Coagulant Dosing Skid sends the Alum Batch Ticket when a new chemical lot is placed into service.
S057: Automatic dose trimming is based on analyzer feedback, operator-entered targets, and verified process response rather than on a single instrument value.
S058: When raw-water turbidity changes quickly, the Duty Engineer may authorize a temporary dose adjustment while the Chief Operator confirms the sustained control point.
S059: The North Filter Gallery, known locally as Cobalt, contains a bank of gravity filters operated from the plant control system.
S060: North Filter Gallery records individual filter effluent turbidity and headloss at the end of each control scan.
S061: South Filter Gallery sends the Filter Run Exception Note when a filter run ends outside the normal operating limits.
S062: Filter run management is based on run time, terminal headloss, effluent turbidity, prior backwash quality, and the current condition of upstream treatment.
S063: A filter is not returned to service after washing until rinse-to-waste quality meets the operating target and the turbidity trend is stable.
S064: If a filter shows an unusual turbidity rise, operating staff compare the analyzer trend with nearby sample results before declaring a process upset.
S065: The Laboratory Technician provides confirmation testing when online analyzers disagree with observed filter performance or with routine process samples.
S066: The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench is used for custody-controlled receipt of compliance and process samples collected from treatment locations.
S067: The SCADA Historian Server retains dose changes, analyzer values, filter status changes, wash sequences, and operator comments for later review.
